extraction.name: Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning that tests the ability of natural language understanding models to link text to a robust intuitive-physics model of the world.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were provided with links to instructables.com to inspire them to create a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid solution (a subtle permutation of the valid one).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The seed data used to prompt annotators consists of how-to instructions from instructables.com, which includes crowdsourced guides for various tasks along with images, videos, and tool lists.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with instructables and asked to create a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid 'trick' solution. The process included a qualification HIT requiring >80% accuracy, and subsequent validation by other annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data was validated by other annotators for correctness. Examples with low agreement were removed, and users with low agreement were disqualified.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: There are some data quality issues where examples marked as errors in the development set are actually correct.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate and diagnose language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense. It is split into training, development, and testing folds.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was preprocessed by truncating examples to a maximum of 150 tokens. Additionally, adversarial filtering (AFLite) was used to produce the dataset splits and handle spurious biases.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we provide a prompt to the annotators derived from instructables.com. The instructables website is a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks. They would then articulate the goal (often centered on atypical materials) and how to achieve it. In addition, we asked them to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid, often subtly... we also include a qualification HIT which contained well constructed and underspecified (goal, solution) pairs. Annotators had to successfully ( >80%) identify which were well formed to participate in the main HIT.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Annotator pay averaged >15$/hr according to both self-reporting onturkerview.com and our timing calculations. [Also references 'HIT design']

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data... Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users will low agreement were de-qualed.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Manual inspection of the development errors show that some “mistakes” are actually correct but required a web-search to verify.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce Physical Interaction: Question Answering, or PIQA to evaluate language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense. [...] the train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite.
